The appointed-promise facet is grounded by the earlier promise in 17:104 and its fulfillment in 17:108.

Each of the seven HFT branch traces matches its supplied root and word index. The faceward and sensory contrast returns through the focus recitation, knowledge, fall, and prostration; 17:108 supplies the answering voice. The HFT roles remain attributed.

The supplied refusal in 17:99, knowledge and insight in 17:102, and the focus recipients' bodily response support the complete knowledge-reception contrast. Each HFT coordinate matches the packet surface; the difference concerns response, not identity between the people in the passages.

All seven HFT trace coordinates match 17:105-107. Truthful descent, division into portions, measured recitation, and the focus fall support the proposed transmission pattern; the recitation-as-following branch is separately grounded by the focus response.

The focus fall, the intervening spoken acknowledgment in 17:108, and the repeated fall, weeping, and increase in humility in 17:109 match every attached HFT trace. The resulting recursive reading is retained as an attributed interpretation, with rhetorical intensification left live.

The 17:110 roots and indices, and the focus speech and recitation coordinates, all match. Its vocal-measure reading fits the adjacent text as an attributed extension, bounded by 17:110's explicit reference to prayer.

The two attributed 17:111 abasement roles, its magnification role, and the focus prostration coordinate all match the supplied surfaces. Their contact bounds human lowering by the coda without assigning a lexical gloss to unresolved HFT branches.

The 17:100 storage, withholding, expenditure, and constriction coordinates match the packet, as do the focus giving and recitation coordinates. The anti-hoarding relation survives as an exploratory analogy about reception, not an equivalence between wealth and knowledge.

findings.title: A response through body, voice, and tears
findings.claim: The focus's prostration belongs to a response that travels through body, voice, and tears: the pericope frames revelation as descending truth read in measured portions, the learned recipients fall at its recitation, answer with spoken glorification and recognition of a fulfilled promise, then fall again with weeping and increased humility.
findings.mechanism: The focus's recitation and sounding fall meet 17:105-106's descent, division, and measured reading. In 17:108, the same recipients speak glorification and name their Lord's promise as fulfilled; 17:109 repeats the fall-on-chins and adds weeping and increased humility. The promise in 17:108 also meets 17:104's promise of the Hereafter, making the spoken response recognition of an announced future event.
findings.reader_payoff: The fall remains a bodily prostration while becoming part of a connected reception: measured recitation reaches the body, receives a spoken answer, and returns as tears and deepening humility.
findings.containment: This is a bounded reading of the supplied pericope sequence. The promise is not identified with an event beyond the supplied wording, and the sound-flow relation does not make every available root image active or replace the ordinary bodily fall.

epistemic.reason: The repeated posture, spoken response, tears, and increase are explicit in the supplied ayat; integrating them as one response is interpretive, and the channel material remains nomination evidence.

The earlier guidance/misguidance contrast in 17:97 frames these as different outcomes without identifying the groups.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's lowering can be seen against the earlier face-down gathering: bodily direction alone does not fix the outcome; recitation, knowledge, and response make a different orientation visible.
findings.containment: The contrast is local to the supplied pericope and does not equate the two groups or claim that the focus explicitly reports restored sight or hearing. The sensory roots remain attributed HFT roles.

findings.title: A measured vocal path
findings.claim: The focus's spoken command and recitation can be heard beside 17:110's instruction to keep prayer voice between loud projection and lowered concealment. The recited message is thus available as a measured vocal practice whose force is received without display or disappearance.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies utterance and recitation; 17:110 supplies calling, the two vocal limits, and a path between them. Their contact extends the focus from semantic content to the register through which recitation reaches its recipients.
findings.reader_payoff: The adjacent instruction makes vocal measure perceptible as part of reception, while preserving the focus's account of what the recipients do when the text is recited.
findings.containment: 17:110 explicitly speaks of prayer, so its transfer to the focus's recitation is an attributed adjacent-context reading. The focus does not state a volume level, and the connection does not turn its recitation into prayer by definition.

epistemic.reason: The traced roots and indices match the supplied surfaces, but the application transfers an instruction about prayer voice to the adjacent recitation and remains an attributed analogy.

findings.title: Lowering without abjection
findings.claim: The focus's prostration can be held beside the closing denial that God needs no ally from abasement and the command to magnify Him. The coda distinguishes the worshippers' lowering as a responsive act from abjection as a condition of need.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies bodily self-lowering. In 17:111, abasement is named as a reason for needing an ally and denied of God, while magnification follows; those exact roles meet the focus posture and bound its reading without removing its physical form.
findings.reader_payoff: The downward posture remains visible as worship while the coda prevents it from being reduced to coerced disgrace.
findings.containment: The relation is attributed to the closing context. It does not claim that 17:111 explains every prostration or that the coda directly describes the focus recipients.

epistemic.reason: The context roots and focus return match the supplied Arabic; the two abasement roles are unresolved HFT nominations and remain attributed.

branch_activations.carrier: At word 19 in 17:111, the supplied trace locates abjection denied as a divine need.

branch_activations.activation: The coda's denied need for protection from abasement meets the focus's bodily lowering.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus posture is distinguishable from the abject dependency named in the coda.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss is supplied; this is an attributed contrast, not a verified lexical facet.

findings.title: Received knowledge beside withheld reserves
findings.claim: 17:100 imagines people withholding from fear of expenditure, while the focus names knowledge as given and recited to its recipients. Their prostration makes reception visible as an answer to what arrives, a bounded counterimage to guarded possession.
findings.mechanism: The traced storage, withholding, expenditure, and constriction in 17:100 meet the focus's passive giving of knowledge, its recitation to recipients, and their bodily response. The contrast changes knowledge from a reserve owned by an elite into something received in an ongoing act of disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast makes the focus's knowledge relational: what is given and recited is met by response, rather than treated as a store held for oneself.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory anti-hoarding analogy across domains. It does not equate mercy with knowledge, claim that the recipients later transmit the text, or establish that they never possess information.

epistemic.reason: The HFT roots and indices match the packet, but the source itself labels this outlier exploratory and explicitly limits it to an analogy about reception.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's knowledge is framed as received disclosure, not a reserve guarded by its recipients.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss is supplied; the storage image remains an attributed contrast.

findings.title: Received knowledge beside bestowed favor
findings.claim: With the external 1:7 overlay, the focus's recipients of knowledge can be heard by analogy beside those upon whom favor is bestowed; their prostration offers a bodily response to something received.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the passive 'they were given knowledge' and its following prostration. The external trigger in 1:7 is 'those upon whom You have bestowed favor.' Both place a recipient group in relation to what is given, making the focus's response a possible illustration while leaving group identity unasserted.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus can be held alongside the Fatiha's request for the path of the favored as an example of received benefit meeting embodied response.
findings.containment: This is an analogical overlay from the individually supplied 1:7. It does not identify the focus recipients with the favored group, define the straight path by this scene, or import the Fatiha's whole-surah theme.

epistemic.reason: The supplied wording provides a concrete recipient-and-gift contact, while the relation between the two groups is analogical and not stated as identity.
